semantics.assignment_replacement: Before DISPATCHED only; arrays are complete active sets; empty array is explicit release-all; released rows are retained; re-add creates a new interval/UUID; identical active set has no mutation.
semantics.responder_uniqueness: Project Owner approved 2026-11-08: one active incident assignment per canonical users.id globally across all organizations. Bind user_id to (organization_id,membership_id) via a composite FK. Enforce atomically with a partial unique index on user_id where released_at IS NULL. Never query across tenants to precheck. Normalize unique conflicts to a stable generic response without identifying other tenant records.
semantics.vehicle_uniqueness: At most one active assignment globally per vehicle UUID; only same-tenant AVAILABLE vehicles eligible; MAINTENANCE/RETIRED ineligible.
semantics.movement: Only contract kinds DEPARTURE/ARRIVAL/RETURN/OTHER. Actor membership and received_at are server-derived. occurred_at remains human reported UTC. Movement rows use immutable logical version 1 and do not increment incident.version. List deterministically by occurred_at, received_at, UUID. New correction record links through supersedes_id; exact replay of same client UUID returns existing representation, reuse with different content is generic 409. No update/delete, invented clock threshold, correction reason, or event-kind-specific authority.
semantics.lifecycle: Only explicit human OPEN→DISPATCHED may be enabled after validating active eligible same-incident responder and AVAILABLE vehicle assignments, tenant scope and no conflicts. DISPATCHED is internal assignment evidence only. ON_SCENE, MONITORING, RETURNING, COMPLETED and CLOSED remain unavailable in Sprint 4. No automatic transition, release, stand-down or vehicle availability change.
semantics.vehicle_state: updateVehicle rejects routine MAINTENANCE/RETIRED state while active assignment exists; no automatic release or new service state.
semantics.change_events: No Sprint 4 extension proposed; existing incident/location event semantics preserved.
semantics.assignment_disposition: Before DISPATCHED, authorized explicit replacement/release follows S4-P-03 and retains interval/audit history. From DISPATCHED onward, responder and vehicle intervals remain active until a separately authorized future resource-release workflow explicitly ends them. Sprint 4 implements no such workflow. Future COMPLETED/CLOSED transitions must be blocked while active intervals remain unresolved. Authority, evidence and transaction semantics for future release remain deferred.

acceptance_tests: Fresh/repeat migration chain; exact three new tables; no historical migration changes; no destructive rollback claim.
Restricted role, RLS/FORCE RLS, no tenant context, cross-tenant reads/writes/references.
Global responder uniqueness across two tenant memberships and generic conflict with no cross-tenant information leak.
Concurrent vehicle assignment across incidents has one winner; concurrent responder assignment across tenants has one winner; losing transactions leave no partial records.
Active membership, vehicle AVAILABLE status, maintenance/retired denial, and setAssignments/updateVehicle race.
Assignment replacement, explicit release-all, no-op, re-add with retained interval history, stale base_version, and post-DISPATCHED change denial.

Movement create/list permissions, actor/received_at derivation, append-only protections, same-incident location and correction lineage projection, deterministic ordering and exact replay/conflicting UUID behavior.
Movement ARRIVAL does not automatically transition status; ON_SCENE and post-dispatch cancellation remain unavailable.
DISPATCHED requires active eligible responder plus active AVAILABLE vehicle, same tenant/incident, explicit command, version CAS, atomic event/audit.
updateVehicle MAINTENANCE/RETIRED guard under concurrent assignment writes.
Real HTTP auth/MFA, tenant/RBAC negative cases, redaction, migration, format/lint/typecheck/build and exact scope/permission parity.
dependencies: global uniqueness implementation and generic error mapping
Q-05/Q-06/Q-08 and production KMS/logging remain open
approval: Project Owner approved global responder uniqueness 2026-11-08; exact scope frozen after successful preflight on 2026-11-08. Sprint 4-A through 4-D are authorized conditionally within this inventory.
stop_rule: Implement only the frozen inventory and explicit bounded dependencies. Stop on new operational ambiguity, security failure, or required scope expansion.

duty_decision.decision: PersonnelAssignment.duty is optional and may be absent or NULL; AssignmentInput remains unchanged; database duty is nullable with no default; no generated/inferred value or invented enum; duty vocabulary/designation deferred; no vehicle-specific crew linkage.

technical_clarifications.decision: From DISPATCHED onward, assignment intervals stay active until a separately authorized future resource-release workflow explicitly ends them. Sprint 4 does not implement release or terminal lifecycle transitions; future COMPLETED/CLOSED must reject unresolved active assignments.
technical_clarifications.scope_effect: Contract/lifecycle clarification only; no table, operation, role or permission added.

scope_freeze.basis: S4-P-01 through S4-P-09 owner approval, explicit S4-P-02 global uniqueness approval, exact 3-table/4-operation reconciliation, and successful documented preflight
